title: Stacked branches with --update-refs
summary: Small pull requests that build on each other, and the one rebase flag that keeps the whole stack in line.

steps.title: A stack of pull requests
body: Big changes review badly. Many teams split them into a **stack**: each branch builds on the one below and gets its own small pull request.
Rebasing the top branch onto `main` copies all four commits, but `stack/1-model` and `stack/2-api` would stay on the old ones: the stack falls apart. Since Git 2.38:
git rebase --update-refs main     # run on the top branch: every branch in the stack moves too
git push --force-with-lease origin stack/1-model stack/2-api stack/3-ui
In `rebase -i` the todo list shows them as `update-ref refs/heads/stack/1-model` lines.

steps.prompt: You run a plain `git rebase main` on `stack/3-ui` (no `--update-refs`). What happens to `stack/1-model`?
options: It stays on the old commit; `stack/3-ui` now holds a copy of that commit with a new hash
Git refuses to rebase because other branches point into the range
steps.explain: A rebase only moves the branch you are on. The lower branches keep pointing at the old commits, so their pull requests no longer match what is in the top one, and the next rebase of each starts conflicting with copies of itself.

steps.title: Move the whole stack
prompt: `~/shop` has a stack of three branches: `stack/1-model` → `stack/2-api` → `stack/3-ui` (you are on the top one). `main` has two new commits.
With **one** rebase, put the whole stack on top of the new `main`, keeping each branch's own commits:

checks.name: stack/1-model sits on the new main
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse stack/1-model^)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/main)" && test "$(git log -1 --format=%s stack/1-model)" = 'Add the coupon model'
checks.fail: `stack/1-model` should be the new `main` plus `Add the coupon model`. A plain rebase leaves it behind; `--update-refs` moves it.

checks.name: stack/2-api sits on stack/1-model
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse stack/2-api^)" = "$(git rev-parse stack/1-model)" && test "$(git log -1 --format=%s stack/2-api)" = 'Add the coupon API'
checks.fail: `stack/2-api` should be `stack/1-model` plus `Add the coupon API`.

checks.name: stack/3-ui sits on stack/2-api
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse stack/3-ui~2)" = "$(git rev-parse stack/2-api)" && test "$(git log --format=%s -2 stack/3-ui | tr '\n' '|')" = 'Label the coupon field|Add the coupon field|'
checks.fail: `stack/3-ui` should be `stack/2-api` plus its two commits.

hints: `git log --oneline --graph --all` shows the stack hanging off the old `main`.
Rebase from the **top** branch, so every lower branch is inside the range.
steps.explain: Git reports `Successfully rebased and updated refs/heads/stack/3-ui` plus one `Updated the following refs with --update-refs` list. Push them all with one `git push --force-with-lease origin stack/1-model stack/2-api stack/3-ui`. When the bottom PR is squash-merged, `git rebase --onto main stack/1-model stack/3-ui --update-refs` drops it from the stack.

steps.prompt: Make every rebase keep stacks together, then publish the moved stack without overwriting anyone's pushes.
code: git push __2__ origin stack/1-model stack/2-api stack/3-ui

steps.prompt: A reviewer asks for a change in the **bottom** PR of your stack. Put the workflow in order.
lines: git commit --fixup=<hash of the model commit>
git push --force-with-lease origin stack/1-model stack/2-api stack/3-ui
steps.explain: Commit the fix anywhere in the stack (the top is easiest) as a `fixup!`; autosquash moves it down to the model commit and `--update-refs` moves every branch above it.
